- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.0) or volatile, model often underestimates or lags behind true price spikes; increase forecast by 1–2% to capture momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots in the next 3–5 days; apply a 1–3% downward correction.
- If true price moves >3% from 10-day moving average, model often fails to mean-revert; adjust forecast to align with 10-day MA unless sentiment strongly contradicts.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to be overly optimistic in early days (e.g., day 1–5) when sentiment is bullish; dampen early forecast values by 0.5–1.5% relative to historical mean.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-period, model often fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment pivot” rule: if sentiment drops below 0.3 after day 10, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for remaining days.
